decision.title: The abstract syntax tree (packet )
decision.summary: The internal XPath abstract syntax tree in src/xpath_ast_internal.h has one node kind per visible grammar production, children tagged by grammar field, and fixed-capacity arrays sized from the concrete syntax tree.

body.p: . src/xpath_ast_internal.h, internal. One node kind per visible production of grammars/xpath (), except comment, and and occurrence_indicator, which only hold a token and become their parent's detail; anonymous field tokens (operator, quantifier, abbreviation) become detail or flags. Children are linked in source order and tagged with their grammar field, so lists are "children with field F" and code finds children by field, never by position: XQuery and pattern grammars, which add node types and add fields to four XPath types, only append to the kind and field enumerations. Nodes and decoded text live in two fixed-capacity arrays () sized from the concrete syntax tree (its node count bounds the AST nodes, the source byte count bounds decoded text), so building never grows; index 0 means "no node". Names are kept as written (prefix, local name, braced URI); string literals and template parts are unescaped and numeric literals lose _ and 0x/0b, while lowering makes the atomic items. Each node has a source span (byte offset and count, line, column in codepoints). Front-end entry points sxml_xpath_build_ast and sxml_xpath_build_sequence_type_ast are declared there and defined by packet in src/xpath_parse.c; the lifecycle and builder functions go in src/xpath_ast.c, also written by 1.16 (the AST module's only producer in Phase 1). Identifiers use the module prefix sxml_ast_, since XQuery and patterns share the tree.
